item.title: Former Bank of England chief economist says Tory growth policies ‘far more likely to succeed’ than Labour’s – UK politics live
item.description: <p>Andy Haldane writes that Conservative economic plans would be best for growth ahead of Healey budget</p><p><strong>Badenoch</strong> says Britain needs tax cuts.</p><p>We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise.</p><p>Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car. You’re taxed when you insure that car. You’re taxed if you take the family away on holiday. You’re taxed if you stay in the UK thanks to Andy Burnham’s tourist tax. You’re taxed to buy a home, taxed to live in a home, taxed to pass on your home. This is clearly not working. Britain does not feel better off.</p><p>Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/20/kemi-badenoch-john-healey-capital-gains-tax-budget-covid-inquiry-care-homes-uk-politics-latest-news">Continue reading...</a>
